title: How flames go out
note: Approved narration (tools/videos/DESIGN.md). Drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); approved by AlanziM2. Editing a recorded script costs ElevenLabs credits.

sentences.say: A flame survives only while it makes heat faster than it loses it.
sentences.show: A flame survives only while it makes heat faster than it loses it.

sentences.say: Lower the oxygen, and the flame makes less heat.
sentences.show: Lower the oxygen, and the flame makes less heat.

sentences.say: At some point the losses win, and the flame goes out on its own.
sentences.show: At some point the losses win, and the flame goes out on its own.

sentences.say: The oxygen level where that happens is called the flammability limit. For choosing cabin materials, it may be the most useful number there is.
sentences.show: The oxygen level where that happens is called the flammability limit. For choosing cabin materials, it may be the most useful number there is.

sentences.say: NASA's FLEX experiment burned hundreds of fuel droplets at different oxygen levels.
sentences.show: NASA's FLEX experiment burned hundreds of fuel droplets at different oxygen levels.

sentences.say: Below fifteen percent oxygen, twenty seven of twenty eight droplet flames went out on their own.
sentences.show: Below fifteen percent oxygen, twenty seven of twenty eight droplet flames went out on their own.

sentences.say: Between thirty and fifty percent, only two of twenty four did. Four kept burning, and the rest were not recorded.
sentences.show: Between thirty and fifty percent, only two of twenty four did. Four kept burning, and the rest were not recorded.

sentences.say: FLEX changed other things too, like the fuel and the pressure, so this is a pattern, not a controlled test of oxygen alone.
sentences.show: FLEX changed other things too, like the fuel and the pressure, so this is a pattern, not a controlled test of oxygen alone.

sentences.say: More oxygen means flames that are harder to stop: the fire risk side of every high oxygen habitat.
sentences.show: More oxygen means flames that are harder to stop: the fire risk side of every high oxygen habitat.
